label: ILN-inspired solar lander
description: Teaching configuration inspired by the NASA ILN Case 1 solar-plus-battery concept. It is not a copy of a flown vehicle, and values marked as project assumptions are not NASA specifications.

landingTime.note: Left empty on purpose; never defaulted to the current time.

durationDays.note: Surface mission length; not the Earth-Moon transit time and never stored in the device configuration.

launchSite.note: Latitude and longitude typed by the user; no default coordinates.

device.pvEfficiency.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): Figure 8.4 (printed p. 59) "Conversion efficiency is 30 percent". Section 5.4.4 (printed p. 37) states a Case 1 "baseline efficiency of 28 percent"; the source is inconsistent and 30 % (Figure 8.4, user-confirmed in v0.7) is used. The only photovoltaic efficiency input (the user's "recharge efficiency").

device.panelCount.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): Figure 8.4 "Two fixed panels (east/west) solar arrays". One east-facing and one west-facing fixed panel.

device.panelWidthM.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): Figure 8.4 "Solar arrays: two 54-by-54-cm".

device.panelHeightM.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): Figure 8.4 "Solar arrays: two 54-by-54-cm".

device.panelTotalAreaM2.note: 2 x 0.54 m x 0.54 m = 0.5832 m2, derived from the Figure 8.4 dimensions. Checked against the three source values when the file is loaded.

device.panelAzimuthsDeg.note: Panel normal azimuth, clockwise from local north: east = 90, west = 270. Derived from "Two fixed panels (east/west)" (Figure 8.4) and "one facing east and the other west" (Section 5.4.5); the source does not state exact azimuths.

device.panelTiltDeg.note: Measured up from the horizontal plane; 90 means vertical. Project value confirmed in v0.7. The source (Section 5.4.5, printed p. 37) states that the Case 1 analysis "assumed two fixed arrays, tilted at 45 deg one facing east and the other west"; this project keeps 90 deg and does not claim it matches the source.

device.pvArrayNominalW.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): Figure 8.3 "Power: 100 W GaAs solar arrays (fixed)". Nominal array power; kept for reference and separate from the controller limit below.

device.pvOutputLimitW.note: The nominal array power (100 W, Figure 8.3, read in the original) is used as the photovoltaic controller output cap on the whole array. This is a project choice; the real controller limit is not stated by the source.

device.baseLoadW.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): "power requirements of 26 W during the day and 23 W during the night" (COMPASS analysis) and "~23 W for payload/housekeeping during lunar night". Electrical load at the device input; applying it for the whole mission is ASM-BASE-LOAD-CONTINUOUS.

device.baseLoadContinuous.note: Applying the night-time load for the whole mission is a project assumption.

device.commLoadW.note: NASA ILN Case 1 report (TM-20210025878), re-read 2026-11-15 from the NTRS PDF (text extracted locally): "Communications: 5 W DC S-band communications ... (average during sunlight periods)". Electrical load at the device input; applying it during every Earth-visible interval is ASM-COMM-ALWAYS-ON.

device.commAlwaysOnWhenEarthVisible.note: Running communication continuously during every geometric Earth-visibility interval is a project assumption. No data rate or minimum downlink is defined.

device.busEfficiency.note: Common power bus to device input only. Applied once to the device load; unrelated to photovoltaic or battery efficiency.

device.batteryCapacityWh.note: Energy at the battery internal storage terminal. Not derived from battery mass.

device.initialEnergyWh.note: Initial stored energy at the internal storage terminal; the battery starts full.

device.reserveFraction.note: Single source of the reserve. The Wh value (2,400 Wh at the default capacity) is derived from this fraction and the capacity, never stored separately.

device.chargeEfficiency.note: Bus to storage. Independent of the other efficiencies.

device.dischargeEfficiency.note: Storage to bus. Independent of the other efficiencies.

device.chargeLimitW.note: Battery charge power limit at the bus.

device.dischargeLimitW.note: Battery discharge power limit at the bus. A net demand above it is an immediate supply failure.

model.solarIrradianceWm2.note: Reference value at 1 AU, to be scaled by the inverse square of the Sun distance. As cited in the project reference file; the fact sheet was not re-read.

model.solarReferenceDistanceAu.note: Distance at which the irradiance above applies. The AU length is the constant already defined in physics/coords.ts and is not repeated here.

model.lossFactor.note: k_loss = 1 only means that dust, temperature and ageing losses are not modelled. It does not claim the real losses are zero.

mission.transitSpeedKmPerS.note: Effective transit speed for a simplified distance-over-time estimate. Chosen by rounding 384,400 km / (3 x 86,400 s) = 1.483 km/s. It is not a measured mean speed of any trajectory.

terrain.footprintDiameterM.note: Local terrain analysis footprint. Not a known ILN lander dimension and not a landing dispersion ellipse.

terrain.slopeLimitDeg.note: Slopes at or above this value are excluded. Project screening value after the ALHAT hazard-detection scale; not a universal NASA landing certification.

terrain.obstacleLimitM.note: Known obstacles at or above this height are excluded. Project screening value; not a universal NASA landing certification.

communication.earthMinElevationDeg.note: Earth counts as visible when the disc centre is above max(terrain horizon, this elevation). Geometry only: no relay, antenna or link budget.

scoring.weightSunlight.note: User-confirmed default in requirements v0.7 section 4. Weights are normalised before use; all zero is invalid. There is no minimum total score.

limits.maxRecommendations.note: Up to this many recommended sites; fewer or none are shown when fewer qualify.

limits.maxCustomSites.note: Custom sites are added to, and never replace, the recommendations.

interaction.timeBase.note: Clock display and inputs use UTC.

interaction.autoplayOnLoad.note: Configuration only; the clock behaviour is implemented in step 16.

interaction.defaultRangeYears.note: Initial timeline range is the load-time instant plus and minus this many UTC calendar years (changed from 10 to 1 at the user's request on 2026-11-15). A display range only: it is not an ephemeris accuracy statement; the step 06 Horizons comparison covers 2016-11-14..2036-11-14.

interaction.clearStartBeforeNowMonths.note: On Clear, when now is before the range start, only the start moves to now minus this many UTC months.

interaction.clearEndAfterNowYears.note: On Clear, when now is after the range end, only the end moves to now plus this many UTC years.

interaction.clearResetsPlaybackSpeed.note: Project detail: Clear restores the default speed.
